author: jessica
_note: TYPE 3, THE TRAIL, the first Delve across THREE places: a note at one POI points to letters at another,
and both go to a third. Three links, then it ends (his: 'ok for the chain to end, otherwise its a
thradmill'). Built by Eliza 2026-10-08; every player-facing word is Jessica's, written 2026-10-08 on his
"yeah 2". The fiction: a soldier's unsent letters, taken home. The natural site is where he left a note,
the military one is where he served, the peopled end is where his sister lives.
2026-10-13, his: "the payoff feels off. Lets change the last to a talk with his sister". The post locker
is gone: the last step is a hand-back TALK (as 11a), so the letters reach a person, not furniture.

place._reach: His 2026-10-13: 'First objective was ages away from the second' ('most of the worldspace'), then 'let's tighten this one quest down to duo_shortdrivedistance'. Every other place within 4,000 of the main place and of each other.
place._theme: The END of the trail, peopled: his sister, placed at the centre.
place._themes: THREE DISJOINT POOLS, so no two links can be one site: the end is peopled (keeping the base's no-natural, no-cave exclusions); the first slate is at an unpeopled NATURAL site; the second at an unpeopled MILITARY one (DROPPED 2026-10-13, his: 'I couldn't test, think the requirements are too narrow. Let's drop the Military keyword req': now any unpeopled, non-natural site, still disjoint from both). Split on the two biggest themes in the pool (gen_delve keywords, 2026-10-08: Natural 121, Military 119); 'infrastructure and not peopled' was 16. Which fiction suits which site is Jessica's call.

prose.name: Search: Soldier's Letters on <Planet>
prose.briefing: I came across a soldier's note pointing to a cache at the <SecondPlace>. Whatever he left there, he never came back for it.

beats.journal: The cache held a note from a private. His letters are stashed at the <ThirdPlace>, and he asks whoever finds this to see they get home.

message.title: Field Note
message.text: The note is folded small and signed with a service number. His letters are stashed at the <ThirdPlace>. Whoever finds this, please get them home.

beats.name: Field Cache

beats.objective: Find the private's letters at the <ThirdPlace>
beats.journal: I've found the private's letters at the <ThirdPlace>. They're all addressed to his sister at the <Place>, so that's where they're going.

message.title: Unsent Letters
message.text: A bundle of slates tied with wire. Every one is addressed to the same person, his sister, at the <Place>. None of them were ever sent.

beats.name: Letter Cache

beats.objective: Take the letters to his sister at the <Place>
beats.journal: I followed a soldier's note from the <SecondPlace> to his letters at the <ThirdPlace>, and gave them to his sister at the <Place>.

person.name: Ilse Corran
hellos: Are you lost? There's nothing out here worth the walk.

greeting: I'd know it anywhere. Where did you find them?

reply: That's every week. He wrote every week.
None of it ever came. I thought he'd stopped.
His unit went quiet near the end of the fighting.
They told us that much and nothing else. I stopped asking.
Ask me once I've read them.

beats._talk: The menu lists exchanges 1 to 3 ABOVE the closer (his play, 2026-10-13), so she sees the letters in the greeting and every question works before the hand-over; the hand-over is the last option, where it reads naturally. Exchange 0 ends the talk, takes the letters and the note, sets stage 100. Voiced: no names, no places. ElevenLabs 'Lucy' (american), heard in game 2026-10-13.
